title: reconcileStuck still SILENTLY DROPS any 'processing' row whose claimed_at is missing/unparseable (Number.isFinite(NaN)===false), and a needs_review row manually re-queued after a submit carries overwritten notes with NO bank fields so it silently vanishes from the fanout — the operator-recovery path round-4 (FIND-101 DEFECT-A) flagged as 'must not be silently dropped' remains a no-alert latent gap.
description: Two residual operator-path gaps, both money-SAFE (no double-pay / no money loss) but defeating the FIND-003 operator-recovery intent: (1) NULL/unparseable claimed_at: reconcileStuck (bank-payout-watcher.mjs:80-81) computes ts=Date.parse(r.ts) and only flags when Number.isFinite(ts). In the normal live flow every 'processing' row IS claim-stamped (claim() line 129 always appends claimed_at), so this is largely unreachable today — but a legacy processing row written before this change, a row hand-set to processing, or a row whose notes got overwritten will have parseClaimedAt(notes)=null -> ts=NaN -> Number.isFinite(NaN)=false -> the row is NEVER flagged and NEVER alerted, sitting stuck in 'processing' forever with no operator signal. Round-4's FIND-101 recommendation explicitly required the NULL case be 'handled by an explicit policy (flag-after-grace or alert), not silently dropped'; the new code still silently drops it. (2) Re-queue of a post-submit needs_review row: once a row reaches 'submitted', buildSubmittedPatch (line 32-35) has OVERWRITTEN notes to `submitted;provider=...;ref=R1`, discarding the bank fields. If an operator (per the FIND-100 design: 'human confirms with GMO then manually re-queues') flips such a row back to 'queued', readBankRecipients->parseBankRecipient sees method!='bank' (the string starts with 'submitted') -> returns null -> the row is silently dropped from the fanout: never re-paid, never errored, no log. The intended manual-recovery action is a no-op, undermining the operator path that is the entire justification for routing failures to needs_review instead of auto-requeue.

evidence.snippet:
if (Number.isFinite(ts) && now - ts >= olderThanMs) { ... }   // NULL/NaN claimed_at -> silently skipped, no alert
buildSubmittedPatch: notes = `submitted;provider=...;ref=R1`   // bank fields gone; a later re-queue parses to null and is dropped

recommendation: For (1): in reconcileStuck, when ts is non-finite emit an explicit alert/flag-after-grace path (e.g. flag rows with no parseable claimed_at after a grace window, or log+counter) rather than silently continuing. For (2): either keep the original bank notes (append, don't overwrite, in buildSubmittedPatch) so a re-queued row remains parseable, or have readBankRecipients/parseBankRecipient log when it drops a row that is NOT a clean email/wallet row so a silent operator-recovery no-op is observable. Add a test for a re-queued post-submit row and a NULL-claimed_at processing row.
